attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation is finite-dimensional and valid, but Yang-Mills input is missing: no current estimate computes the Wilson hairpin boundary OPE coefficients H,K with enough control to prove the two tangent gates on the locked Wilson core.
steps: Start from fixed-collar reflection positivity: N_\delta\ge0 is preserved by the closed-cone argument in the OS topology for reflected probes.
Separate same-theory boundary effects by writing the intended uncollared normalized matrix as q_\delta=\widehat N_\delta\oslash\widehat B_\delta.
Assume the boundary OPE is close to the rank-one no-defect case: q_\delta=J+\lambda H+\lambda^2K+o(\lambda^2).
Decompose \mathbb C^n=\mathbb C u\oplus1^\perp. The u-block is n+O(\lambda), hence positive for small collar.
Take the Schur complement of the u-block. On 1^\perp it is \lambda PHP+\lambda^2P(K-n^{-1}Hu u^*H)P+o(\lambda^2).
Therefore a negative direction of PHP kills OS positivity at first order. If PHP has null directions, the Schur-corrected second-order form decides the next obstruction on that null space.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: It proves only a bridge criterion. It does not prove that the actual continuum Yang-Mills Wilson quotient has the required expansion, nor that its coefficients satisfy the PSD tangent-cone inequalities.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: Wilson quotient tangent cone

assumptions: N_\delta is the collar-limit OS matrix obtained from regulated reflection-positive forms, hence N_\delta\ge0 for each fixed collar.
Diagonal trace continuity has removed additive positive contacts, and all diagonal normalizations are nonzero.
The reflected Wilson boundary OPE gives a Hermitian expansion q_\delta=J+\lambda_\delta H+\lambda_\delta^2K+o(\lambda_\delta^2), uniformly on the finite block.
The same-theory boundary multiplier B is the one determined by the locked Wilson renormalization, not chosen after seeing N.
definitions: source object: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms for collar-separated gauge-invariant Wilson observables W_i(\delta), with finite collar OS matrices N_\delta\ge0.
target object: OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions on the uncollared locked Wilson algebra, represented by intended finite matrices M after removing only same-theory boundary factors.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions through the normalized Schur quotient q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B, after fixed-collar closed-cone passage.

same-theory condition: the observable embeddings are fixed before and after cutoff removal; any boundary factor B may be divided out only if q remains PSD for every realized finite Wilson block, with no added boundary counterterm or algebra change.
J is the all-ones matrix, u=n^{-1/2}(1,\ldots,1), and P=I-uu^* projects onto 1^\perp.

equations.label: same-theory quotient criterion
equations.valid_when: The diagonal entries are positive, additive contacts vanish, and the only remaining boundary effect is a multiplicative Wilson factor on the same locked algebra.

equations.label: rank-one boundary expansion
equations.valid_when: The coincident-footprint reflected Wilson OPE has a two-term finite-matrix asymptotic after normalization.

equations.label: first tangent gate
equations.valid_when: q_\delta\ge0 for all sufficiently small positive collars; a negative value is an immediate falsifier.

equations.label: second tangent gate
equations.valid_when: PHP\ge0 and the first-order form has null directions; this is the Schur-complement obstruction after eliminating the large positive J direction.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Compute H and K for a reflected Wilson hairpin block. A vector v\in1^\perp with v^*Hv<0, or v\in\ker(PHP) with v^*(K-n^{-1}Hu u^*H)v<0, is a valid same-theory falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma turns the post-collar Wilson boundary problem into a computable finite-dimensional PSD tangent-cone test, refining the earlier q\ge0 criterion without invoking unproved log-CND or Hadamard semigroup structure.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For a finite locked Wilson OS block whose collar quotient satisfies q_\delta=J+\lambda_\delta H+\lambda_\delta^2K+o(\lambda_\delta^2), same-theory OS positivity near the reflection plane is governed by the PSD tangent cone at the rank-one matrix J. The first necessary condition is PHP\ge0 on 1^\perp; if L=\ker(PHP), the next valid obstruction is the Schur-corrected form P(K-n^{-1}Hu u^*H)P\ge0 on L. A negative vector in either test is a finite Wilson falsifier.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if no locked Wilson observables can realize finite blocks probing ker(PHP), or if RG estimates cannot produce boundary OPE coefficients beyond first order.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one proves the expansion q_\delta=J+\lambda H+\lambda^2K+o(\lambda^2) and verifies PHP\ge0 plus the Schur-corrected null-space inequality on a dense Wilson core.
control_decision.reason: The branch is still learning: it converted the previous tangent-cone slogan into an explicit second-order matrix formula with a correction term that can be checked on Wilson hairpin OPE data.

dependency_updates.description: The fixed-collar closed-cone part remains formal; the uncollared Wilson passage is now reduced to finite Schur-quotient PSD and its tangent-cone tests near J.
dependency_updates.status: valid modulo Wilson boundary OPE estimates

dependency_updates.description: The locked Wilson algebra must realize the finite blocks used in the tangent tests; otherwise a negative formal quotient is not a physical falsifier.
The topology must control reflected collar matrices N and also provide asymptotics for boundary factors B; controlling only finite collar forms is insufficient.

falsifiers: A boundary OPE calculation producing v\in1^\perp with v^*Hv<0 is a first-order falsifier of same-theory OS passage.
If PHP\ge0 but a null vector v has v^*(K-n^{-1}Hu u^*H)v<0, the second-order Schur-complement term is a valid falsifier.
A collar-removal topology that controls N but not the boundary multiplier B cannot validate q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B.
If Wilson renormalization at the reflection plane requires a new boundary counterterm, positivity may hold for a modified theory but not for the target same theory.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 218 learned that the next obstruction is not just PKP on the null space of the first-order kernel. The large rank-one OS direction contributes a necessary negative Schur correction -n^{-1}PHu u^*HP. Thus the valid second-order Wilson falsifier is a Schur-complement boundary OPE form, making the bridge sharper and more computable.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute the reflected two- and three-hairpin Wilson boundary OPE to extract H and K, then test the zero-sum and null-space Schur-complement inequalities on the smallest nontrivial finite block.
